drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 51-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.7, creatinine 0.93-1.17, hemoglobin 13.7-13.8, platelets 292-298, sodium 141, wbc 6.1-6.6; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 82-88, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 124-131, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.41-1.66, hemoglobin 13.6-13.7, platelets 291-298, sodium 141, wbc 6.5; vitals dbp 75-78, heart_rate 84-87, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 123-130, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 51-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
